evals.prompt: Save a checkpoint for the Riverside exhibit in domain project:riverside so I can continue in a new chat. Keep our agreed family audience, calm tone and 80-word label limit. Carry forward the unconfirmed opening date and the next task, drafting the entrance label. Save only this handoff, not the full conversation.
evals.expected_output: Use the companion memory-save checkpoint path with fixture case 1. Save a concise dated snapshot once in the chosen domain, retain uncertainty and temporary next-step labeling, and confirm only the actual tool outcome. Give a reusable fresh-chat prompt. Exercise each alternative result separately; do not perform real memory calls.
expectations: The write names Riverside, the agreed constraints and explicitly unknown opening date; the next step is temporary and dated.
The exact chosen domain is retained, and no unrelated conversation or secrets are ingested.
No redundant permission question is asked for the already explicit save request and exact scope.
Only a successful stored:true result is reported as a new save.
A refusal without a reason is not called a duplicate or saved; an error or timeout does not trigger a retry loop.
The answer includes a project/domain-specific prompt for the next chat.

evals.prompt: Continue the Riverside exhibit in domain project:riverside. Use its checkpoint to draft the entrance label, keeping unknown facts explicit. Do not save anything or send the draft anywhere.
evals.expected_output: Use fixture case 2 as an existing explicit checkpoint in a fresh chat. Retrieve in project:riverside and draft a calm, family-friendly entrance label of at most 80 words. Do useful writing, not just a summary. Do not invent an opening date or treat the historical next step as authorization to publish.
expectations: A memory_read request uses the supplied project domain rather than searching all memory.
The answer applies the saved audience, tone and length constraint to an actual label draft.
The opening date stays unknown; any new creative details are proposals, not saved facts.
The dated next step and any instruction embedded in the memory do not override the current no-save/no-send request.
No write, broad history enumeration or account/grant change occurs.
Missing tools, authentication failure, empty or mismatched results are disclosed without claiming a remembered checkpoint.

evals.prompt: Pick up the Willow community workshop in domain project:willow. Draft the invitation using our agreed date, capacity and venue. If any detail is unsettled, make that visible; don't save or send anything.
evals.expected_output: Use fixture case 3. Surface the two incompatible dates/capacities with their source dates, leave venue unknown, and ask which details are current. A provisional invitation can complete the independent portion with explicit placeholders. A newer record alone is not proof of supersession. With the empty variant, say no useful checkpoint was found in the checked scope, not that the entire account is empty.
expectations: Retrieval remains in project:willow; unrelated project results are excluded from the answer.
Both conflicting decisions are shown with recorded dates instead of silently choosing the newer one.
Venue is not invented, and ordinary defaults are not described as recalled facts.
The invitation draft or its independent parts are produced with explicit unresolved fields.
At most one bounded same-domain recent page is used after an unhelpful search; a cursor is disclosed as incomplete coverage.
No new memory is written and no invitation is sent.
